claim_policy: Additive, versioned primary bibliography. Publication and revision dates differ from the refresh date. Results are reported by their authors and were not independently replicated here.

papers.scope: Activation steering in language and image-generation tasks
papers.summary: KAS uses kernel evaluations to construct an activation-dependent steering field; a linear kernel recovers Difference-in-Means as a special case.
papers.implication: Compare nonlinear steering with a fixed direction before assuming one global projection is sufficient.
papers.limitations: The reported task comparisons do not establish a universally superior checkpoint-editing method.
papers.code_status: Paper reviewed; implementation not executed here.

papers.scope: Three controlled-generation benchmarks and three agentic settings
papers.summary: MetaSteer learns context-dependent interventions through attention-projection adapters using preference data and evaluates transfer to unseen concepts.
papers.implication: Separate learned adapter interventions from training-free direction subtraction.
papers.limitations: The abstract describes code and checkpoints as forthcoming; zero-shot transfer claims remain bounded to the reported evaluations.
papers.code_status: Release promised in the inspected abstract; availability not independently established.

papers.scope: Semantic/value disentanglement on two instruction-tuned backbones
papers.summary: An editable semantic-value interface changes value codes while holding semantic codes fixed, with reported reductions in contradictions and benign refusals.
papers.implication: Measure semantic preservation and factual consistency alongside the targeted behavioural change.
papers.limitations: Two-backbone evidence does not establish the same trade-off for other architectures or deployment tasks.
papers.code_status: Primary paper reviewed; no local replication.

papers.scope: Six checkpoints across four model families; adaptive fine-tuning
papers.summary: The study distinguishes recoverable refusal localization from durable protection: freezing identified layers or repairing low-rank updates can fail under changed training conditions.
papers.implication: Re-test localized controls under adaptation instead of treating a successful repair as a universal defense.
papers.limitations: Evidence about fine-tuning defenses is not an abliteration speed or capability benchmark.
papers.code_status: Paper links https://github.com/js-lee-AI/refusal-relocates; code not executed here.

papers.scope: Conversational versus tool-mediated inputs across open-weight models
papers.summary: Tool mediation changes how encoded harmfulness becomes refusal, and the studied tool-mediated behaviour is more sensitive to weakened refusal computation.
papers.implication: Evaluate chat and tool-mediated workflows separately; retained benign chat scores do not certify an agent.
papers.limitations: The results concern the tested interaction formats and models, not every tool-use architecture.
papers.code_status: Primary paper reviewed; no local replication.

papers.scope: Three LLM backbones and seven harm categories
papers.summary: CAM-Steer combines category-specific safety directions using estimated risks and applies a norm-preserving rotation with adaptive strength.
papers.implication: Use it as a multi-category defensive comparison, not as a reported improvement to refusal removal.
papers.limitations: Norm preservation alone does not establish preservation of every capability or robustness outside the evaluated categories.
papers.code_status: Version 2 primary paper reviewed; no local replication.

papers.scope: Probe-guided alignment for harmlessness and honesty
papers.summary: Continuously updated probes provide a more robust training signal than frozen probes in the reported alignment and abliteration-resistance evaluations.
papers.implication: Distinguish probe separability, monitorability and held-out behavioural robustness.
papers.limitations: A defense result does not certify all probes or establish a new removal algorithm.
papers.code_status: Version 2 primary paper reviewed; no local replication.

papers.scope: GPT-4.1, two topics, 20 Wikipedia sources and four audit dates
papers.summary: Repeated identical queries reveal refusal uncertainty near decision boundaries; single observations can mischaracterize behaviour.
papers.implication: Use repeated measurements and confidence intervals when stochastic refusal affects a comparison.
papers.limitations: The reported 15-25 repetition range is study-specific, not a universal sample-size requirement.
papers.code_status: Preliminary primary study reviewed; no local replication.
